$comment: The exact migration set of this release, split into the two phases the
expand/contract procedure applies separately, with a content hash for each
file. This is the artifact that makes the split executable from the exact
tree: scripts/db-phase-push.mjs applies one named phase and nothing else, and
scripts/check-release-manifest.mjs keeps the manifest equal to the directory.
Round-4 review C6 asked for `required_for_app` and `deferred_contract` sets
that the claimed, remote and pending sets must exactly equal, plus runtime
posture checks; C7 asked for a tested exact-hash phase tool that records
correct migration history without moving files or rewriting history.
hash_algorithm: sha256 over the file's UTF-8 content with CRLF normalised to
LF, which is also the text the phase tool sends to the server, so the hash
covers exactly what is executed and does not depend on the checkout's line
Nothing here asserts that anything has been applied. See

required_for_app.$comment: State 2 of supabase/preflight/expand-contract-rollback.md §2: the schema the candidate needs is present and the release mode is still the compatible one, because the previous release is still the deployed one. One posture claim is deliberately NOT here: whether the migration owner can actually clear auth.sessions/auth.refresh_tokens. A predicate for it would have to name the DML privilege, which this gate forbids in a posture query for good reason, and 20260817120000 asserts it at apply time instead — so the phase push fails on the migration rather than passing the apply and failing the readback.

predicates.name: release-mode-row-is-compat
predicates.sql: select coalesce((select direct_write_mode = 'compat' from public.money_release_mode where id = 'only'), false)

predicates.name: money-rpcs-are-installed
predicates.sql: select count(*) = 7 from (values ('create_contract'),('approve_contract'),('revoke_contract'),('confirm_payment'),('allocate_payment'),('void_payment'),('convert_quotation_to_contract')) as r(n) where exists (select 1 from pg_proc p join pg_namespace n on n.oid = p.pronamespace where n.nspname = 'public' and p.proname = r.n)

predicates.name: write-guards-are-installed
predicates.sql: select count(*) = 4 from (values ('trg_guard_contracts_write'),('trg_guard_payments_write'),('trg_guard_quotations_write'),('trg_guard_contract_transition')) as t(n) where exists (select 1 from pg_trigger g where not g.tgisinternal and g.tgname = t.n)

predicates.name: gate-function-is-security-invoker
predicates.sql: select not p.prosecdef from pg_proc p join pg_namespace n on n.oid = p.pronamespace where n.nspname = 'public' and p.proname = 'money_direct_write_is_blocked'

predicates.name: mode-function-is-security-definer
predicates.sql: select p.prosecdef from pg_proc p join pg_namespace n on n.oid = p.pronamespace where n.nspname = 'public' and p.proname = 'money_direct_write_mode'

predicates.name: session-revocation-rpc-is-server-only
predicates.sql: select has_function_privilege('service_role', 'public.revoke_user_sessions(uuid, text)', 'execute') and not has_function_privilege('authenticated', 'public.revoke_user_sessions(uuid, text)', 'execute') and not has_function_privilege('anon', 'public.revoke_user_sessions(uuid, text)', 'execute')

deferred_contract.$comment: State 4: direct end-user money writes are refused. This is past the rollback boundary for the previous release; see §5.

predicates.name: release-mode-row-is-strict
predicates.sql: select coalesce((select direct_write_mode = 'strict' from public.money_release_mode where id = 'only'), false)

predicates.name: write-guards-are-still-installed
predicates.sql: select count(*) = 4 from (values ('trg_guard_contracts_write'),('trg_guard_payments_write'),('trg_guard_quotations_write'),('trg_guard_contract_transition')) as t(n) where exists (select 1 from pg_trigger g where not g.tgisinternal and g.tgname = t.n)
